Route 16 - Engine bay main routes (surgical rewire)

Status (Dan, 2026-10-21): APPROVED as drawn, names approved. Every new engine-bay circuit runs along one of these 9 lines (DECISIONS B9: no OEM wire crosses into the engine bay; every engine-bay circuit is new wire on one main route). This set replaces the engine-bay paths in Routes 1 to 4; those files are retired in the surgical-rewire repo sweep (OPEN-ITEMS row 164).

Redrawn clean from Dan's markup (2026-10-21) on the 1993 EWD "Electrical Wiring Routing" p.36 (3S-GTE). Best fit on factory art, not measured. Firewall at top, front at bottom, passenger (RH) side on the left. Route 9 dashed = runs low, behind the engine.

#NamePath
1Main trunkBulkhead (RH firewall, in the spot of the large OEM accordion grommet pass-through, near the new fuse boxes in the glove box area; Dan 2026-10-25) across the firewall to the driver side.
2Driver-side dropDown the driver side to the old J/B No.2 spot.
3Passenger fender dropRH firewall corner down the passenger inner fender.
4Passenger front runDown the passenger side, then across the front.
5Driver firewall spurDriver-side firewall corner to the trunk.
6Belt-end dropDown the timing-belt end of the engine.
7Head loom, rearAcross the head, firewall side.
8Head loom, frontAcross the head, radiator side.
9Alt and starterIn at the RH firewall, then low behind the engine (dashed) to the alternator (left branch) and the starter (right branch).

Device spots and branches (Dan, 2026-10-28)

The one definition of where each engine-bay device of the ECU engine harness sits and which line it hangs on. Placed by Dan in the placement editor on the same EWD page; the drawing tree and wire lengths are made from this table. MR-S pump plugs B / C (24 / 25) carry harness C circuits that ride this loom from the bulkhead; plug A (power) is harness C at the same pump. L1-L9 = routes 1-9; L9b / L9c = route 9 low parts (starter / alternator); N1-N19 = device branches.
